title: Cyclic Induction for ZMod n — Adapt Induction to Cyclic Structures

problemStatement.formal:
\forall n \geq 1,\; \forall P : \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \to \text{Prop},\quad
P(0) \;\wedge\; \bigl(\forall k,\; P(k) \to P(k+1)\bigr) \;\implies\; \forall k,\; P(k)
problemStatement.plain: Standard mathematical induction works for natural numbers: prove P(0), prove P(n) → P(n+1), conclude ∀n, P(n). But ℤ/nℤ is a finite cyclic group — you can keep adding 1 and eventually wrap back to 0. Does an analogous "cyclic induction" principle hold?
